Let me analyze this certificate.

Certificate: R76/2006-DK3-14.06, Member State Denmark, issuing authority DELTA, OIML Issuing Authority DK3. Date issued: 21 October 2014. Page total: 2.

Scheme: R76-1? Actually R76 has parts 1 and 2; the certificate says R76 edition 2006, accuracy class III. Scheme A or B — not specified. The schema asks for scheme (A|B) in certificate. Not stated; omit or null. I'll omit.

Project number: DK3? Not clear. The certificate number is R76/2006-DK3-14.06. DK3 is the issuing authority ID. OIML issuer ID: DK3.

Issuing authority: DELTA, address Venlighedsvej 4, 2970 Hørsholm, Denmark. Person responsible: J. Hovgård Jensen, title Certification Officer. Phone: +45 7219 4000. Email: legal@delta.dk. Website: www.madebydelta.com. OIML issuer ID: DK3.

Applicant: Kaifeng Group Co., Ltd., No 6-8, Shifang Middle Road, Gushan Town, Yongkang City, Zhejiang 321307, CHINA.

Manufacturer: Kaifeng Group Co., Ltd. (same address presumably).

Certified type: category "Non-automatic weighing instrument" (Indicator? No — it's a complete instrument). Type designations: ACS-C, ACS-L2, ACS-L5, BL-CN, ACS-R, BL-GN, ACS-A1, ACS-268, ACS-568, ACS-668A, ACS-668B, ACS-768, ACS-868. That's 13 types.

Description: "Intended to be used for direct sales to the public."

Recommendation: R76, edition 2006, accuracy_classes ["III"]. Scheme: R76 is for NAWS — not scheme A/B. Omit scheme? The schema says scheme (A|B) in certificate — that's about OIML-CS certification scheme A or B, not the recommendation. Not stated; omit.

Test reports: 
- DANAK-1913671, dated 12-12-2013, 68 pages, from DELTA, DK. role: type_evaluation_report
- DANAK-1914393, dated 12-08-2014, 20 pages, from DELTA, DK.

Model family: The cert covers multiple types but no model-attribute matrix per model. The characteristics table lists Max 3 kg to 30 kg as a range — that could be across models. Hmm. "Maximum capacity Max: 3 kg to 30 kg". This is a range across the family of types. Should I create model_level? We don't know per-model Max. It's a range at type level covering all models. I'll keep it as type_level with range {min: 3, max: 30}, unit kg.

Since cert covers >1 model variant (13 types), include model_family with models listed by type designation. family_name: null.

Characteristics type_level:
- accuracy_class: III (string) — value "III"
- weighing_range: "Single-interval or dual-range"
- maximum_capacity: {min: 3, max: 30}, unit kg
- minimum_capacity: "20 e" — value 20, unit "e"? The unit here is "e" (verification scale interval). value: 20, unit_symbol: "e". Actually "20 e" means 20 verification scale intervals. So value 20, unit "e".
- verification_scale_interval: {min: 1, max: null}, unit "g" (≥ 1 g)
- max_intervals: ≤3000 → {min: null, max: 3000}, unit null (dimensionless). Attribute: Max_i / e_i → "max_intervals" (number of intervals). Canonical: "number_of_intervals" or "max_intervals". Use "max_intervals"? The label says "Number of intervals Max_i/e_i". Canonical snake_case: "max_intervals". I'll use "max_intervals".
- subtractive_tare: ≤ -Max → value "-Max" string? "T ≤ -Max". Value is "-Max" as string, symbol: "-Max"? It's a formula. Keep value: "-Max" string, unit null. Hmm, actually "Subtractive tare T ≤ -Max" meaning subtractive tare range is up to -Max. I'll record {"value": "-Max", "unit_symbol": null}.
- interface: "None" → value "None". Maybe include as "interface".
- supply_voltage: 220 VAC → value 220, unit "V". power supply frequency 50 Hz. Also optional internal battery → separate: "power_supply_options": "internal battery (optional)".
- temperature_range: {min: -10, max: 40}, unit "°C", attribute "temperature_range_for_indicator" or canonical "operating_temperature_range_indicator". Use "temperature_range_indicator".
- software_identification: "120305".

Footnote markers: none.

Revision history: none.

Footnotes: none.

Components: none.

Matrix tables: none.

Now the type_level structured values must be objects with value/unit_symbol/unit_id. For strings like accuracy class III: {"value": "III", "unit_symbol": null, "unit_id": null}.

Weighing range: value "Single-interval or dual-range".

Should model_family be included? Schema: "include ONLY if cert covers >1 model variant". 13 type designations — yes. models[] each with model_id = type designation. But are these type designations rather than models? The schema also says certified_type.type_designations should list all. And model_family for variants. I'll include model_family with the 13 types as model_ids, family_name null.

Test report dates: "dated 12-12-2013" — ambiguous DD-MM-YYYY (Danish). 12-12-2013 → 2013-12-12. "dated 12-08-2014" → Danish format → 12 August 2014 → 2014-08-12. I'll output as given? Better ISO: "2013-12-12" and "2014-08-12". Danish convention day-month-year. I'll use ISO with that interpretation.

Certificate date_issued: 21 October 2014 → 2014-10-21.

oiml_issuer_id: DK3 (DELTA, OIML Issuing Authority DK3).

Scheme: The schema says scheme (A|B) under certificate — OIML-CS scheme. Not mentioned in the doc; 2006-era certificates predate scheme A/B labeling. Omit.

page_total: 2.

Category: "Non-automatic weighing instrument". Module designation: not applicable — it's a complete instrument; the identification says "Non-automatic weighing instrument". module_designation: null or "Not applicable". I'd set null... The schema allows "Not applicable" | null. I'll use null.
